sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: Landmarks or areas having **cultural, historical, scientific**, or other forms of significance, legally protected by international treaties.
**UNESCO** (**United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization**), headquartered in **Paris, France**.
Established under the **World Heritage Convention** adopted in **1972** (India ratified it in **1977**).
**43 Sites** in total (as of **2024**), making India home to the **6th largest** number of World Heritage sites in the world.
**34 Cultural Sites**, **7 Natural Sites**, and **2 Mixed Sites** (**Khangchendzonga National Park**).
**Moidams** (Assam) under Cultural category and **Santiniketan** (West Bengal) / **Sacred Ensembles of Hoysalas** (Karnataka) in recent cycles.
Questions frequently target **first sites**, **latest additions**, **UP-specific sites** (**Taj Mahal, Fatehpur Sikri, Agra Fort**), and **Natural sites**.

items.title: Category 1: Cultural Heritage Sites
items.content:
• Includes **monuments, groups of buildings, and sites** having outstanding universal value from historical, aesthetic, archaeological, or anthropological points of view.
• India has **34 Cultural sites**.
• Examples: **Taj Mahal** (Uttar Pradesh), **Red Fort Complex** (Delhi), **Sun Temple** (Konark), **Hampi Monuments** (Karnataka).
• **Mnemonic for Top Cultural Sites:** "**TAFHS**" -> **T**aj Mahal, **A**janta, **F**atehpur Sikri, **H**ampi, **S**anchi.

items.title: Category 2: Natural Heritage Sites
items.content:
• Includes **natural features, geological formations, strictly delineated zones**, and natural sites of outstanding universal value from science, conservation, or natural beauty.
• India has **7 Natural sites**.
• Examples: **Kaziranga National Park** (Assam), **Sundarbans National Park** (West Bengal), **Western Ghats**, **Great Himalayan National Park** (Himachal Pradesh).
• **Mnemonic for Natural Sites:** "**KSMWG**" -> **K**aziranga, **S**undarbans, **M**anas, **W**estern Ghats, **G**reat Himalayan.

items.title: Category 3: Mixed Heritage Sites
items.content:
• Properties that contain elements of **both natural and cultural significance**.
• Globally, there are very few mixed sites; India has **only 1 Mixed site**.
• Site Name: **Khangchendzonga National Park** located in **Sikkim** (inscribed in **2016**).
• Features both unique biodiversity (snow leopards, red pandas) and profound religious/cultural significance for indigenous communities.

items.title: Selection Process and Criteria
items.content:
• Proposals are submitted by member states through a **Tentative List**.
• Evaluated by advisory bodies: **ICOMOS** (for cultural sites) and **IUCN** (for natural sites).
• Final decision is made by the **World Heritage Committee** meeting annually.
• Must meet at least one of **10 selection criteria** (Criteria i to vi for cultural, vii to x for natural).

items.title: Intangible Cultural Heritage of India
items.content:
• Distinct from tangible heritage sites, UNESCO also recognizes **Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH)**.
• India has **15 intangible cultural elements** inscribed.
• Recent additions include **Garba** (Gujarat) in **2023** and **Durga Puja** (Kolkata) in **2021**.
• Other examples: **Kumbh Mela**, **Vedic Chanting**, **Yoga**, **Ramlila**.

items.definition: **T.A.F.** -> **T**aj Mahal, **A**gra Fort, **F**atehpur Sikri. All 3 are located in **Agra, Uttar Pradesh** and were among the earliest Indian sites inscribed in **1983** and **1986**.
**A.A.E.T.** -> **A**janta, **A**gra Fort, **E**llora, **T**aj Mahal. Remember: "**All Animals Eat Tamarind**" for A-A-E-T.
**K.M.S.** -> **K**aziranga, **M**anas, **S**undarbans. These three are iconic eastern natural biodiversity hotspots inscribed in **1985** and **1987**.
Only **1** mixed site in India. Think **K**hangchendzonga = **K**ing of Mixed sites located in **Sikkim**.
Remember **34-7-1** rule: **34** Cultural, **7** Natural, **1** Mixed, making a total of **42** standard heritage entries (plus recent updates reaching **43**).

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing Mixed Site with Natural Site
items.definition: Students often think Sundarbans or Kaziranga are mixed sites. **Correction:** Only **Khangchendzonga National Park** is a Mixed Heritage site in India.

items.term: Mistake 2: Number of UP Heritage Sites
items.definition: Students forget **Fatehpur Sikri** or confuse the total count. **Correction:** Uttar Pradesh has **3** primary UNESCO World Heritage monuments (Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri).

items.term: Mistake 3: Year of World Heritage Convention
items.definition: Confusing the **1972** convention establishment year with India's ratification year (**1977**) or first inscription year (**1983**).
Treating intangible elements like **Kumbh Mela** or **Durga Puja** as built heritage sites. **Correction:** They belong to the **Intangible Cultural Heritage** list, not physical monuments.
Assuming all national parks are UNESCO sites. **Correction:** India has over 100 national parks, but only **7** are designated as UNESCO Natural World Heritage Sites.
India features **43 UNESCO World Heritage Sites** as of 2024.
Comprises **34 Cultural**, **7 Natural**, and **2 Mixed** (including recent expansions) sites.
**Ajanta Caves**, **Ellora Caves**, **Agra Fort**, and **Taj Mahal** were India's first inclusions.
Key UP sites include **Taj Mahal** (1983), **Agra Fort** (1983), and **Fatehpur Sikri** (1986).
India holds the **6th position** globally in terms of total number of World Heritage sites.
**Khangchendzonga National Park** in **Sikkim** is India's sole mixed heritage property.
Includes **Kaziranga**, **Manas**, **Sundarbans**, **Keoladeo**, **Nanda Devi**, **Western Ghats**, and **Great Himalayan National Park**.

upscNotes.content: For the UP Assistant Teacher exam, focus heavily on Uttar Pradesh-specific sites (Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri) along with the first sites (1983) and the sole mixed site (Khangchendzonga).
Keep track of the latest additions (like Moidams in Assam) as current affairs questions in Environmental and Social Studies frequently tap into newly inscribed heritage sites.
Do not confuse Ramsar wetlands or Biosphere reserves with UNESCO World Heritage sites; while some overlap exists (e.g., Sundarbans, Kaziranga), their classification criteria differ.
Avoid mixing up Intangible Cultural Heritage elements (like Yoga or Kumbh) with physical Cultural Heritage monuments when asked about site counts.

keyTakeaways: India has 43 UNESCO World Heritage Sites: 34 Cultural, 7 Natural, and 2 Mixed.
The first sites were inscribed in 1983: Ajanta, Ellora, Agra Fort, and Taj Mahal.
Uttar Pradesh hosts 3 major World Heritage monuments: Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, and Fatehpur Sikri.
Khangchendzonga National Park in Sikkim is India's only Mixed Heritage site.
UNESCO is headquartered in Paris, France, and operates under the 1972 World Heritage Convention.
India ranks 6th globally in terms of total World Heritage property listings.
